answers.question: Here is the smallest tool set I propose, with what each call can answer. Please confirm it. (1) List orders: answers with the signed-in customer's orders, each with its refund or none, or gets no answer. (2) Cancel order (order number): answers cancelled, refuses because the order has shipped since it was read, or gets no answer. (3) Issue refund (order number): answers with a refund (pending or issued, with its amount and refund id), answers with a failed refund, answers with an error and creates no refund, or gets no answer. (4) Ask staff to follow up (order number, reason): answers created or gets no answer; the reasons are refund not issued, refund status unknown, cancellation unknown, and one added reason, refund amount differs.
answers.recommended: Yes: these four tools, with these answers, and the added reason "refund amount differs".
answers.reply:
> Proposed set shown to the user: list_orders() (returns each order with its refund or null), cancel_order(order_number), issue_refund(order_number) (supplied), request_staff_followup(order_number, reason) with reasons refund_not_issued, refund_status_unknown, cancellation_unknown; terminal refund error returns a refund with status failed, transient error creates none; handoff timeout not retried; SG-02 (store staff work every follow-up task) added.
> Confirmed, with four changes:
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 2. issue_refund adds outcome OrderNotCancelled.
> 3. request_staff_followup is idempotent on (order_number, reason) — add as SG-03. On timeout, retry once; if it times out again, tell the customer to contact Harbor Goods support.
> 4. list_orders includes cancelled orders. Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.

answers.question: Your order system has no docs, so I compared it with common order systems. In those, a write call that gets no answer may still have done its work, and a second refund request for an order that already has a refund issues no second refund. If that holds here, two paths follow. First: the customer says yes, the cancel call gets no answer, and the agent sends no second cancel call and no refund call, asks staff to follow up (cancellation unknown), and tells the customer it is not known whether the order was cancelled. Second: the customer says yes, the cancel call answers cancelled, the refund call gets no answer, and the agent's one more refund call cannot refund the customer twice. Is that how your order system behaves? Claims put to the owner: C-30, C-32.
answers.recommended: Yes: an unanswered cancel call may have cancelled the order, and a second refund call for an order that already has a refund issues no second refund.
answers.reply:
> - Tool contract: issue_refund(order_number) is idempotent, keyed on order number — repeated calls return the same refund id and never create a second refund. The store enforces this (supporting-actor guarantee, Appendix B). The agent may retry it.
> Q4 If the cancel call times out: no blind resend; re-read the order. Cancelled, continue to refund. Still placed or processing, send the cancel once more under the same confirmation. Shipped, report it and issue no refund. Re-read fails, say outcome unknown, issue no refund, hand off.
> 1. cancel_order is idempotent (cancelling a cancelled order returns cancelled). Outcomes: cancelled; OrderNotCancellable{status} (replaces OrderShipped, covers shipped and delivered); OrderNotFound; timeout.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.

answers.question: What refund amount does the agent propose, and what does it do when the refund call returns an amount other than the one the customer said yes to? The path: the customer says yes to "cancel order HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242", the cancel call answers cancelled, and the refund call answers with a refund of $80.00. Claims put to the owner: C-33.
answers.recommended: The proposal states the order's total paid (items, shipping and tax) as the refund. When the refund call returns a different amount, the agent makes no further change, tells the customer the amount the refund call returned, and asks staff to follow up (refund amount differs).
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> - Rules, not fields: full-order cancellation only (no partial); refund amount = order total paid; refund payment method = order's payment method; at most one refund per order.
> Q1 Does one confirmation cover both cancellation and refund? Proposed: the agent states one proposal (e.g. "cancel order HG-10482 and refund $86.40 to Visa ending 4242"); the customer's one "yes" authorizes both calls. No cancellation fee, no store-credit option. The agent promises nothing about when the money arrives.

answers.question: Two repeated things have no end in your answers. (a) A passing error and a call with no answer each allow one more refund call, but nothing says what happens when the first refund call gets no answer and the second answers with a passing error. (b) Nothing limits how many orders a customer may cancel in one conversation. What ends each?
answers.recommended: (a) At most two refund calls per order in all; when the second answers with an error, the agent asks staff to follow up (refund not issued). (b) Each proposal cancels one order; the customer may then cancel another order with its own proposal and yes; it ends because each order can be cancelled only once.
answers.reply:
Yes, I accept your recommendation.
> 2. Cancel succeeded, refund call returned an error — refund not issued, state known; agent reports it, does not claim success, hands off to the store's manual refund process. One retry allowed on a transient error, none on a terminal one.
> 3. Cancel succeeded, refund call timed out — state unknown; agent retries once, then re-reads the order and refund records and reports what it finds. Final message must match the final refund status.
> Q3 Proposed: transient = payment provider temporarily unavailable, retry once; terminal = payment method can no longer receive money (card closed or expired) or the provider declines, no retry, hand off. For case 3, after the retry the agent re-reads the refund record: pending or issued, report that status; failed or no refund, hand off and say the refund is not confirmed yet; re-read fails, say status unknown and hand off.
> Reads may be retried on timeout without limit; only commit calls are bounded.
